assessments.reasoning: On printed p. 18 the opening requirement associates each value of the index type with its own component. The grammar defines the index type as ordinal and the component type through a type denoter. Example 1 gives a subrange index with real components and a Boolean index with colour components. The written one-entry condition fits this mapping and also applies when the component denoter is itself an array type.

challenge.method: Inspect the replica cover and the §6.4.3.2 raster. Test the R1 wording with the comma-separated Example 2, then expand its brackets and consider only an outer Boolean index. Test R2 with both the shorthand and the separately nested spelling, where the outer declaration has exactly one written index.
challenge.results: The comma-separated Example 2 is excluded from R2 by its written index-list length. Its nested equivalent has a one-entry outer list, and an outer Boolean value reaches the entire remaining two-level array. The real component is reached at the innermost level. R1's wider wording lets the reader attach a single index value to the trailing written real type, which the example defeats. The exact R2 claim uses the component type denoted at the applicable level and survives the counterexample.

limitations: This is the logical one-index mapping in the exact unextended ISO/IEC 7185:1990 online replica. The cover gives the printed edition precedence on a discrepancy. Separate rules govern shorthand expansion, packing, storage representation, bounds, and conformant-array parameters. Extended Pascal and vendor dialects require their own evidence.
